case_title: Satya Narayana Tiwari And Anr. v. State of U.P.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.304-B, s.498-A; Dowry Prohibition Act s.4
aggravating_circumstances: Demand for dowry, persistent harassment, cruelty, burning and strangulation
neutral_facts: The accused, a husband and his mother-in-law, were charged with the death of a bride who died of strangulation and burn injuries in her matrimonial home. The deceased, aged about 24 years, died within three years of her marriage. The father of the deceased stated in the FIR that dowry was being demanded, specifically a Maruti car. The trial court acquitted the accused, but the High Court convicted them under sections 304-B and 498-A of the IPC and section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act. The deceased was subjected to harassment and maltreatment by the accused due to the demand for dowry, which persisted after about six months of marriage. The deceased was found in her bedroom with signs of violence, including ligature marks and burn injuries. The accused were found to have committed the crime, with the mother-in-law falsely reporting the death as a suicide. The prosecution established that the accused caused the death through strangulation and burning, which was a case of dowry death.
